name: When should I consider a full remodel instead of repairing my existing kitchen?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider a full remodel instead of repairing my existing kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should plan a full remodel when your current layout hinders daily cooking, storage is inadequate, or underlying components are failing. Warning signs include water-damaged subfloors under the sink, outdated electrical panels that cannot support modern appliances, or deteriorating cabinet boxes. If simple repairs no longer resolve persistent issues, a full overhaul allows you to reconfigure work zones, incorporate modern accessibility or storage features, and upgrade electrical and plumbing lines to current residential standards in one coordinated effort.
acceptedAnswer.description: A full remodel is recommended when the layout no longer works, storage is lacking, or structural, electrical, or plumbing systems require replacement.
